skill.name: literature-review
skill.description: Create systematic literature reviews with structured search planning, citation verification, search result processing, and markdown-to-PDF document generation.
skill.summary: Build systematic literature reviews with search workflows, verified citations, and formatted outputs.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, academic search terminology, and public reference links. Confirmed risks include pandoc execution on user-supplied inputs, unconstrained report writes, and expected DOI metadata requests. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Pandoc receives user-controlled paths without option guarding.
remediation.suggestion: Reject filenames beginning with a dash, insert -- before input paths, and restrict template and output paths to the project workspace.

remediation.issue: Scripts write output files without destination constraints.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit output paths, warn before overwriting existing files, and keep generated reports inside the current workspace.

remediation.issue: Citation verification makes outbound DOI and Crossref requests.
remediation.suggestion: Document the network domains, request user confirmation before verification, and provide an offline mode for sensitive drafts.

remediation.issue: Setup guidance uses unpinned package installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions where practical and separate optional setup commands from the main review workflow.

- Use `gget` skill: `gget search biorxiv "search terms"` for preprints
- Use `bioservices` skill for ChEMBL, KEGG, UniProt, etc.
- Choose one citation style and use throughout (see `references/citation_styles.md`)
- **PDB**: `gget` or direct API for experimental structures

- `assets/review_template.md`: Complete literature review template with all sections

semantic_findings.title: Pandoc Argument Injection Risk
semantic_findings.description: scripts/generate_pdf.py passes the user-provided markdown file directly to pandoc without a -- delimiter or option-like filename rejection. A crafted filename beginning with -- can be interpreted as a pandoc option.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command list includes markdown_file before fixed pandoc options and does not add -- before user-controlled paths. The risk depends on crafted local filenames, so confidence is high but not maximal.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Installation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs users to install Python and system packages without version pins. This can change host state and fetch latest packages from external repositories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The installation commands are explicitly documented for pip, brew, and apt-get. The commands are setup guidance, not automatic execution, which limits the severity.

content.value_statement: Literature reviews require careful searches, screening, citation checks, and reproducible documentation. This skill structures the workflow and prepares polished markdown or PDF outputs.
actual_capabilities: Guides systematic review planning with PICO, scope, databases, and inclusion criteria.
Documents search strategies for PubMed, bioRxiv, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, and biomedical sources.
Processes search result files by deduplicating, filtering by year, ranking, and exporting formats.
Verifies DOI metadata through DOI and Crossref services, then writes a citation report.
Generates PDF output from markdown through pandoc when local dependencies are installed.
limitations: Does not retrieve paywalled full text without user-provided access.
Network citation checks send DOI values to public DOI and Crossref services.
PDF generation depends on local pandoc and xelatex installations.
Review quality still depends on user screening and domain expertise.

use_cases.title: Plan a Systematic Review
use_cases.description: Define the research question, databases, search terms, screening stages, and quality assessment before searching.

use_cases.title: Organize Thesis Sources
use_cases.description: Turn exported citations into deduplicated, themed literature notes with verified references.

use_cases.title: Document Search Methods
use_cases.description: Create reproducible search strategy sections with dates, result counts, and database-specific syntax.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structured literature review on [topic]. Use PubMed, preprint servers, and Semantic Scholar. Include search terms and citation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a systematic review protocol for [question]. Define PICO, inclusion criteria, databases, screening stages, quality assessment, and outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize findings from these search results: [paste citations]. Deduplicate entries, group themes, flag evidence quality, and prepare a review outline.

prompt_templates.title: Map Evidence Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Conduct an advanced evidence map for [domain]. Compare database coverage, identify gaps, plan citation chaining, and prepare reproducible methods.

output_examples.input: Review recent CRISPR therapies for sickle cell disease.
output: Structured review outline with research question, databases, and inclusion criteria.
Search strategy table with PubMed, bioRxiv, and Semantic Scholar coverage.
Thematic synthesis sections with verified citation notes and PDF generation steps.

output_examples.input: Check citations in a completed markdown review.
output: DOI verification summary with verified and failed references.
Formatted citation suggestions in APA style.
A saved report file for audit and correction work.

output_examples.input: Prepare a thesis literature review draft from exported search results.
output: Deduplicated source list with year filtering and ranking.
Theme-based organization for the results section.
Reproducible methods text with search dates and database counts.

best_practices: Document every database, search string, date, filter, and result count before screening.
Use at least three complementary databases and include synonyms for each core concept.
Verify citations and review generated PDFs before sharing or submitting the work.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on one database for a comprehensive or systematic review.
Do not treat preprints as peer-reviewed evidence without clear labeling.
Do not publish generated synthesis without human screening and quality assessment.

faq.question: Does it search databases automatically?
faq.answer: It guides searches and can process exported result files. Some database access depends on other tools or manual exports.

faq.question: Can it create a publishable PDF?
faq.answer: It can generate a PDF from markdown when pandoc and xelatex are installed locally.

faq.question: Does it verify citations?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled verifier checks DOI resolution and Crossref metadata for citations in a markdown file.

faq.question: Is it suitable for systematic reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes PRISMA-style documentation, screening steps, and quality assessment guidance.

faq.question: Does it replace expert review?
faq.answer: No. It supports workflow and formatting, but users must judge study quality and conclusions.

faq.question: What data leaves my machine?
faq.answer: Citation verification sends DOI values to DOI.org and Crossref. Other network searches depend on chosen database tools.
